question: Should Discord Activity support continue from this older core-path draft, move to the newer overlapping Discord Activities pull request, or restart as a Canvas-plugin-owned design with fail-closed Activity auth?
rationale: The unresolved choice crosses plugin ownership, Gateway authorization, token transport, operator config shape, and overlapping open branches, so automation can identify defects but should not choose the permanent Activity security boundary.

options.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
options.body: Port the work to extensions/canvas and extensions/discord, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

options.title: Continue through the newer PR
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/65205 only after its similar security, compatibility, proof, and merge-state blockers are resolved.

options.title: Pause Activity support
options.body: Leave Discord Activities out of core until maintainers settle whether this belongs in the Canvas plugin, Discord plugin, or an external package.

recommendation.title: Rebuild under Canvas plugin auth
recommendation.body: Port the work to extensions/canvas and extensions/discord, require explicit Activity credentials, avoid URL tokens, bound fanout, and add live Discord proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The blocking decision is primarily about Gateway auth, config migration, and Canvas plugin ownership, where current-main history points most strongly to this owner.
